title: Design docs, ADRs and reviews
summary: The interview skills at work: a design doc that reviewers can approve, ADRs for single decisions, the questions seniors ask in review, and the production readiness review before launch.

steps.title: The design doc
body: At work, the system design interview becomes a **design doc**: a few pages written before building
anything big, so that people can disagree cheaply, on paper, instead of expensively, in code. A common outline:
```text
# Design: <feature>
## Context                 why now; the problem in the users' words; links
## Goals                   what must be true when this is done (with numbers)
## Non-goals               what we deliberately will not do (prevents scope creep in review)
## Estimates               QPS, storage, bandwidth, growth: with units
## Proposal                the design: diagrams, API, data model, main flows
## Alternatives considered at least two, and why they lost
## Security and privacy    authn/z, personal data, retention, threat model
## Observability           SLIs and SLOs, dashboards, alerts
## Cost                    monthly estimate and what drives it
## Rollout                 flags, stages, migration, and how to roll back
## Open questions          what reviewers should help decide
Write it for the reviewer who has ten minutes: the first page should say the problem, the decision and the
main trade-off. Keep the doc short and the numbers honest; a doc that hides its weak points gets a slower
review, not a faster one.

steps.prompt: Put these design doc sections in the usual order.
steps.explain: Problem before solution: context, goals and non-goals frame what "good" means; estimates size it; the proposal and its alternatives come next; rollout closes, because how you ship depends on what you built.

steps.prompt: Why does a design doc have a **Non-goals** section?
options: To agree up front what will not be built, so reviewers do not block the design for missing things that were never in scope
To list the features that failed in the previous version
To record the reviewers who disagreed
To keep a backlog of bugs
steps.explain: "Supports video albums?" is a review comment that can stall a doc for a week. "Non-goal: video albums (next quarter)" answers it before anyone asks.

steps.title: ADRs: one decision, one page
body: A design doc covers a whole feature and is mostly read before the work. An **architecture decision record**
(ADR) records one significant decision so that people joining later understand *why*:
```text
ADR 0012: Use a queue between the upload API and the thumbnail workers
Status:   Accepted (2026-11-03)        Proposed -> Accepted -> Superseded by ADR 0031
Context:  uploads spike 5x in the evening; thumbnails take ~2 s of CPU
Decision: publish an event per upload; workers consume at their own rate
Consequences: thumbnails can lag by minutes at peak; consumers must be idempotent
ADRs live next to the code (`docs/adr/0012-upload-queue.md`), are never edited after acceptance (a new ADR
supersedes an old one), and take ten minutes to write. The Messaging topic has a worked example in
*Cloud anti-patterns and the ADR* (`messaging/09-choosing-a-broker`).
Rule of thumb: a design doc when the work is weeks and touches several teams; an ADR for every decision that
would be expensive to reverse.

steps.prompt: Match each document to its job.
pairs: Proposes a whole feature or system before it is built, for review
Records one significant decision and its consequences, forever
Checks a service is safe to run before it takes real traffic
Step-by-step actions for on-call when an alert fires
Explains an incident and the action items that prevent a repeat

steps.title: The reviewer's checklist, and the readiness review
body: Seniors ask the same questions in every design review. Answer them in the doc and the review is short:
- What are the numbers, and where is the bottleneck at 10x?
- What happens when each dependency is slow, down, or returns garbage? Is every retry safe (idempotent)?
- Where is the data, who owns it, how is it backed up, and how long is it kept?
- How will we know it is broken (SLIs, alerts), before customers tell us?
- How do we roll it out, and how do we roll it **back**, including the data migration?
- What does it cost per month, and what makes the cost grow?
Before launch, a **production readiness review** (PRR) checks the built service, not the idea: SLOs defined and
dashboards live, alerts routed to an on-call rotation with runbooks, load tested at the expected peak plus
headroom, backups restored at least once, capacity spread across zones, dependencies' limits known, and a
rollback tested.

steps.prompt: Is this a design review question or a production readiness check?
items: Why a queue rather than calling the thumbnail service directly?
Alerts page the on-call rotation and each links to a runbook
Which alternatives were considered, and why did they lose?
A restore from last night's backup was tested
Is the bottleneck at 10x the database or the cache?
A load test reached the expected peak plus headroom

prompt: **Symptom first.** A new albums feature launched at 10:00. At 10:20 album pages fail for 8% of users. The
team decides to turn the feature off, but the deploy had already run a migration that renamed a column the old
code still reads. The outage lasts two hours. Which part of the design doc would most likely have prevented
options: A rollout section with a rollback plan: expand-then-contract migrations (add the new column, dual-write, switch reads, drop the old one later) so turning the flag off is safe
More boxes in the architecture diagram
explain: The design may have been fine; the rollout was one-way. A rollback plan forces the question "can the old code
run against the new schema?", which leads to expand-then-contract migrations and a feature flag that can

steps.title: A design doc linter
prompt: Write `List<string> Lint(string[] doc)` for Markdown design docs. A section starts with a line that begins
with `## ` (after trimming); its title is the rest of the line, trimmed. Lines until the next `## ` belong to
that section; lines before the first section are ignored. Compare titles **ignoring case**.
1. For each required section, in this order, that is missing: `"missing: <title>"`. Required:
2. If there **is** a `Rollout` section but none of its lines contains `rollback` or `roll back` (any case):
A complete doc gives an empty list.
solution: else if (current is not null && line.Length > 0) current.Add(line);
hints: Build a `Dictionary<string, List<string>>` with `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`, adding lines to the current section.
Then check each required title with `ContainsKey`, and the Rollout lines with `Contains(..., StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoGood = new[] {
"# Design: shared albums",
"## Context", "Users ask for albums.",
"## Goals", "- Album page p99 under 300 ms.",
"## Non-goals", "- Video albums.",
"## Proposal", "- Albums table keyed by album_id.",
"## Alternatives considered", "- A document store.", "- Tags instead of albums.",
"## Rollout", "- Feature flag at 1%, 10%, 100%.", "- Rollback: turn the flag off; the schema change is additive." };
Dojo.Eq("a complete doc", new List<string>(), Lint(dojoGood));
var dojoBad = new[] {
"# Design: shared albums",
"## Context", "Users ask for albums.",
"## Goals", "- Albums.",
"## Proposal", "- A new table.",
"## Rollout", "- Ship it on Monday." };
Dojo.Eq("missing sections and no rollback", new List<string> { "missing: Non-goals", "missing: Alternatives considered", "no rollback plan" }, Lint(dojoBad));
var dojoNoRollout = new[] { "## context", "x", "## GOALS", "x", "## Non-goals", "x", "## Proposal", "x", "## Alternatives considered", "x" };
Dojo.Eq("titles ignore case; no Rollout means only one problem", new List<string> { "missing: Rollout" }, Lint(dojoNoRollout));
var dojoRollBack = new[] { "## Context", "## Goals", "## Non-goals", "## Proposal", "## Alternatives considered", "## Rollout", "  We can Roll Back by redeploying v41.  " };
Dojo.Eq("'roll back' in any case counts", new List<string>(), Lint(dojoRollBack));
var dojoSub = new[] { "## Context", "### Rollout", "## Goals", "## Non-goals", "## Proposal", "## Alternatives considered" };
Dojo.Eq("a ### heading is not a section", new List<string> { "missing: Rollout" }, Lint(dojoSub));
